walkthroughs.body_html:
Development of Practical Skills — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Development of Practical Skills brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Development of Practical Skills.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A car travels 4 km north then 3 km east. What is its displacement magnitude?
options: 7 km
5 km
1 km
25 km

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
options: Acceleration
Momentum
Kinetic energy
Weight

mcqs.q: Does light always travel at the same speed?
options: Charge was created by friction and pulled the balloon to the wall.
No — light always slows with distance from its source.
Yes — c is a universal constant in every situation.
Only in a vacuum; in any material medium (water, glass) light travels more slowly, which is what causes refraction.

mcqs.q: When you rub a balloon and stick it to the wall, what has been transferred?
options: Electrons have been transferred between the balloon and the cloth (not the wall).
No — light always slows with distance from its source.
Protons jumped from the balloon to the wall, causing static cling.
Charge was created by friction and pulled the balloon to the wall.

mcqs.q: Do all stars end their lives as supernovae?
options: No — only sufficiently massive stars (above about 8 solar masses) explode as supernovae; lower-mass stars become white dwarfs.
Yes — every star eventually explodes.
Charge was created by friction and pulled the balloon to the wall.
Yes — but only after billions of years on Earth's scale.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Velocity”?
options: Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Scalar”?
options: Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resolving vectors”?
options: Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Vector”?
options: Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Acceleration”?
options: Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Displacement”?
options: A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
